summary: Rabbi Yosei says the holiest korbanos may be shechted on top of the mizbeach, as if it were the north side. The menachos had their kometz taken anywhere in the courtyard and were eaten by male Kohanim until midnight.
stIntro: It was taught in the previous chapter that offerings of the most sacred order are to be slaughtered in the northern section of the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: The holiest korbanos that were shechted on top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: With regard to offerings of the most sacred order that one slaughtered atop the altar,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: it is as if they were shechted in the north.
chunks.st: Their status is as though they were slaughtered in the north, and the offerings are therefore valid.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei the son of Yehudah says,

chunks.en: from the middle of the mizbeach to the north is like the north; from the middle of the mizbeach to the south
chunks.st: The status of the area from the halfway point of the altar and to the south is like that of the south, and offerings of the most sacred order slaughtered in that area are therefore disqualified. The status of the area from the halfway point of the altar and to the north is like that of the north.

chunks.en: and they are eaten inside the curtains by male Kohanim,
chunks.st: and were consumed within the area enclosed by the curtains by males of the priesthood,

chunks.st: prepared in any form of food preparation that he chooses, e.g., roasted or boiled,

chunks.en: for a day and a night, until midnight.
chunks.st: for one day and night, until midnight.

summary: The bird chatas was done at the southwest corner of the mizbeach. That corner was used for three things below the red line and three things above it.
